# Oxelis plugins (for AI assistants that write plugins)

Oxelis is a screen translator/OCR tool. Plugins are JavaScript run in QuickJS, one sandbox per plugin.
A plugin = folder with manifest.json + main.js. Copy templates/hello-translate and edit.

Rules that matter:
- main.js is CommonJS: `module.exports = class X { onload(oxelis) { ... } }`. The only global is `oxelis`.
- No require, no fs, no setTimeout, no fetch, no TextEncoder. Use oxelis.http.fetch (blocking) or oxelis.http.fetchAll (parallel, up to 4).
- https only, and only hosts listed in manifest permissions.net (exact name or "*.suffix"), or the host of a setting named in permissions.netFromSettings.
- Translators: oxelis.services.translate.register({ id, name, translate(texts, from, to) }). Return an array of strings, same length as texts. May be async.
- Settings: declare in manifest "settings" ([{key,label,secret,default}]), read with oxelis.settings.get(key). Never hard-code secrets.
- Limits: 48 MB memory, 60 s per call.
- Wired today: log, http, settings, translate, and the editor: oxelis.ui.addButton/addPanel/hide, oxelis.theme.set, oxelis.layout.set, oxelis.app.{notify,copy,run,text,translation,selection,lines}, oxelis.on('selection'|'ocr'|'translated').
- A plugin that adds to the editor MUST list it in manifest "provides": ["buttons","panels","theme","layout","events"], or it is not started there. Copying to the clipboard needs permissions.clipboard=true.
- The 'ocr' handler receives {lines, source} and may return a new array of lines (post-processing before display).
- Registered but not used yet: ocr services, commands.
- Types: sdk/oxelis.d.ts. API description: docs/plugin-api.md. Examples: official/*/main.js.
